## 固定收益開篇主論點

8月14日美國固定收益市場收盤，推翻了消費數據疲弱必然帶動債市上漲的直觀解讀。2年期美國公債殖利率收高2個基點至4.17%，5年期上升4個基點至4.36%，10年期上升5個基點至4.68%，30年期上升4個基點至5.25%。2s10s曲線陡化3個基點至51個基點，2s30s擴大2個基點至108個基點。7月零售銷售與8月消費者信心起初降低聯準會近期升息的可能性，2年期殖利率一度跌破4.10%；但油價再受衝擊，加上市場持續要求更高補償以承接財政供給帶來的存續期間風險，政策面的利多未能延續。

本輪賣壓的結構凸顯市場矛盾。7月零售銷售下降0.6%，創2025年5月以來最大跌幅，13個類別中有5個下滑；密西根大學8月消費者信心初值降至51，低於市場共識55。芝加哥聯準銀行總裁Austan Goolsbee肯定近期通膨改善並主張耐心觀望，但強調通膨連續5或6個月朝錯誤方向發展後，仍需再看到數月有利數據。這些發展削弱近期升息的理由。然而，美國財政部長Scott Bessent承諾對伊朗施加史無前例的經濟壓力，伊朗港口也持續遭封鎖，WTI因而上漲1.42%至$82.40，布蘭特原油上漲1.67%至$88.52。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升3個基點至2.27%，10年期實質殖利率上升2個基點至2.41%；通膨補償與實質折現率雙雙推高名目殖利率。

這是同時傳達兩層訊息的熊市趨陡，並不代表成長數據已無關緊要。短端仍對消費與招聘轉弱敏感，9月升息預期也較7月底大幅下降。較長天期債券則須消化能源溢價、仍偏高的最終通膨水準，以及本週10年期與30年期標售雖獲適度承接，卻仍未化解的財政融資定價問題。過去1個月，30年期殖利率已上升17個基點，2年期則下降1個基點，2s30s曲線同期陡化18個基點。聯準會近期路徑轉趨溫和，正與長期資本成本上升並存。

信用市場仍正常運作，但價格紀律明顯轉強。投資級發行人此前兩週已發債$1,360億；承銷團收窄最終定價後，投資人平均撤回36%的初始訂單，流失率為前一週的兩倍，也遠高於全年平均22%。週四45%的流失率更創2026年新高。與此同時，基金流入近$30億，投資級債平均利差仍維持在美國公債上方約78個基點。這不是資金出逃，而是投資人手中雖有現金，但主權債、AI基礎建設與併購融資同時爭奪資產負債表空間，使投資人更不願放棄新券讓利。

同樣的差異也延伸至較低評級與結構型信用。AI融資正從一般公司債轉向專案債與特殊目的載體，並由殘值擔保支撐；產業下行時，這些擔保可能轉為實際義務。另一方面，Liberty Puerto Rico債權人擴大法律訴訟，挑戰以其聲稱已被移出可追索範圍的資產作擔保之融資；另有多家借款人選擇增資、出售資產或重整，而非仰賴低成本再融資。因此，本交易日美國公債殖利率上升，反映市場正更廣泛地重估由誰承擔長存續期間、科技淘汰與擔保品移轉風險。市場仍然開放，但損失如何分配已更具關鍵性。

## 消費疲弱遭遇新一輪通膨衝擊

消費數據無論幅度或廣度都削弱近期升息理由。7月零售銷售下降0.6%，且未經通膨調整。網路與其他非店面銷售下降2.2%，汽車與零件銷售額下滑1.8%。餐廳與酒吧是報告中唯一的服務類別，成長0.5%，使整體數據不至於成為全面收縮訊號。時點因素也須納入考量，因Amazon今年將Prime Day從去年的7月提前至6月，可能使部分網路消費提前發生。即使有此扭曲，降幅仍相當廣泛，顯示上半年表現較強的消費者已不如先前有韌性。

密西根大學消費者信心初值降至51，低於市場預估中位數55，增添另一項疲弱訊號。配合不如預期的就業數據，以及7月溫和的消費者與生產者通膨，這批數據加速了8月7日開始的政策重定價。短期利率合約僅反映9月約升息8個基點，低於7月31日的近19個基點；交易員也逐步撤回截至2027年中升息超過1次的押注。2年期美國公債殖利率一度跌破4.10%，創6月30日以來最低，正是政策預期轉變最直接的市場反應，午後才告反轉。

Goolsbee提出的反應函數框架，支持耐心觀望，但不代表可以自滿。他形容經濟與勞動市場基本穩定，並表示若零售銷售連續數月下滑，將令他擔憂；不過，通膨仍是他的首要關切。此前5或6個月數據不利，過去3個月的表現則令他鼓舞；若再有3或4次類似6月的數據，他將更確信通膨正回到2%。因此，他支持7月按兵不動，是以累積更多確認為前提，而非僅憑一份疲弱消費報告。聯準會7月已連續第5次會議維持利率不變，3位決策官員則主張升息25個基點並投下反對票；即使市場定價轉向再度暫停升息，決策陣營仍有分歧。

生產力又使政策訊號更為複雜。Goolsbee指出，去年數據較強後，生產力已放緩，並質疑這波疲弱是否只是暫時現象。AI帶動生產力加速，可能容許經濟在不引發通膨的情況下更強勁成長；但也可能刺激大量投資，使需求過熱。因此，同一輪科技週期既可能長期降低單位成本，也可能推升當前資本支出、電力與融資需求。單月零售疲弱縮小了立即收緊政策的理由，卻無法判定經濟供給能力是否改善得足以承接AI投資熱潮。

油價使偏鴿訊號無法主導收盤。Bessent表示，美國將於次週公布經濟孤立史上前所未見的措施，同時持續以海軍封鎖伊朗港口。布蘭特原油收於$88.52，1週上漲5.95%；WTI收於$82.40，同期上漲5.40%。美方威脅在收盤前出現，抵銷了稍早疲弱需求數據帶來的債市漲勢。相較股市僅小幅下跌，債市對能源與通膨風險的反應更直接：S&P 500下跌0.17%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.13%，VIX則下跌2.60%至14.25。

通膨連結市場清楚呈現能源衝擊的傳導。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升3個基點至2.27%，完全收復前一日跌幅，回到8月11日水準；10年期實質殖利率也上升2個基點至2.41%。因此，名目債券賣壓既非單純由油價推動，也不只是期限溢價上升。通膨補償反映地緣政治再度推高能源風險，實質殖利率則在公私部門大量舉債之際，維持偏高的資本門檻。黃金上漲0.39%至$4,380.40，美元指數下跌0.29%至99.67，顯示避險需求持續，但未出現美元融資緊縮。

收盤殖利率曲線比任何單一標題都更能解釋這組矛盾。消費疲弱降低聯準會立即升息機率，但油價上漲提高等待成本，財政供給則持續壓抑長天期債券。5年期殖利率上升4個基點、10年期上升5個基點，顯示壓力並非只在最長端。不過，2s10s與2s30s斜率走陡，仍清楚區分政策與存續期間風險：不確定性已從下一次會議，移向通膨路徑、實質資本成本，以及長期債務所需的融資價格。

## 長存續期間仍須高價才能完成定價

週五賣壓延續此前美國公債標售帶來的訊息，無須重述完整結果。$420億10年期與$250億30年期公債均獲市場承接，長債投標倍數大致正常，但得標殖利率分別創2007年與2001年以來最高。融資管道仍暢通，問題在於成本：債務存量擴大、赤字持續，加上邊際買方對價格更敏感，使通膨數據即使暫時改善，市場仍要求更高補償。

30年期殖利率收於5.25%，高於標售得標殖利率5.216%；10年期回到4.68%，幾乎正好是其標售完成定價的水準。過去1個月，10年期殖利率上升10個基點，30年期上升17個基點，2年期則下降1個基點。因此，2s10s斜率51個基點與2s30s斜率108個基點，不只是押注未來降息，也包含額外存續期間溢價：短端通膨降溫並未降低政府融資需求，投資人因而要求更多補償。

實質殖利率結構進一步確認這項負擔。10年期實質殖利率為2.41%，過去1個月上升8個基點；30年期實質殖利率達3.00%，同期上升13個基點。投資人所獲補償不只針對通膨不確定性；公共赤字、AI資本支出與全球政府舉債共同爭奪儲蓄，使實質折現率本身也已上升。30年期固定房貸利率達6.69%，為2025年7月以來最高，顯示即使聯準會下一步行動的威脅下降，主權債融資價格仍會傳導至家庭財務。

Fitch維持AA+評等，並未消除財政回饋循環。該機構警告，減稅與關稅退稅將使2026年赤字占GDP比率擴大。本財政年度迄今利息支出已達$1.17兆，較上年同期增加15%，美國公債殖利率走高也是推升因素。借款成本上升會擴大利息支出，進而增加未來融資需求。美國財政部將債務管理措辭從評估未來標售規模「增加」，改為考慮「調整」，開啟減少長債供給的可能性，但目前尚未減量。將更多發行移至2年至7年期，雖可改變存續期間分布，卻會提高再融資曝險，並不能消除赤字。

現券交易量足以使本次收盤具代表性，但無法據此判定客戶流向。美國公債成交額以原始面額計達$9,745億，較異常活躍的前一交易日低19.0%，其中名目附息債占$8,244億。20年以上天期成交$1,168億，即使整體交易下降，仍較前一日增加3.3%；交易商對客戶交易占該天期50.7%。因此，長端殖利率上升是在存續期間持續雙向移轉下形成，而非源於市場缺乏交易。

即將標售的$160億20年期公債，將提供下一個直接的融資定價觀察。該券週五成交殖利率約5.25%，發行前交易殖利率約5.27%。若標售得標殖利率接近此水準，將創該天期自2020年恢復發行以來最高。此事件屬於下一交易日，而非已完成的收盤；但其起始水準已顯示，美國消費轉弱與9月升息預期下降，幾乎未讓長端保留任何利多。

## 信用資金仍充裕，但新券讓利再度重要

投資級初級市場已從輕易收窄發行利差，轉為投資人明顯抵抗。本週平均訂單流失率達36%，是前一週的兩倍，並高出2026年平均14個百分點；週四45%更創全年新高。AMD發行$47.5億債券時，發行人降低借款成本後，最長天期券種的訂單減少逾半。交易仍順利完成，但也顯示利差收窄後，帳面訂單規模高估了最終需求。

供給背景足以解釋投資人行為轉變。借款人兩週內已發行$1,360億，使8月可望成為歷來發行量最大的8月，之後一週預計降溫至約$200億。併購融資與AI基礎建設需求，連同一般再融資，同時面對實質殖利率已偏高的美國公債曲線。投資人仍可承接發行日程，但主權債、公司債與專案債的選擇增加，接受極低新券讓利的機會成本也隨之上升。

整體市場狀況仍然平穩。截至週三的1週內，投資級債基金流入近$30億，平均投資級利差約為美國公債上方78個基點。週五HYG與JNK僅分別下跌0.10%與0.07%，過去1週仍小幅上漲；LQD則因基準殖利率上升而下跌0.40%。基金價格無法確認現券利差方向，但與全面拋售信用資產並不一致。較合理的解讀是，承銷市場已轉為買方市場；投資級債總報酬疲弱主要來自存續期間，個別發行條件則決定訂單能否留存。

AI融資使這種選擇性具有結構性重要性。Nvidia擬與Goldman Sachs、Blackstone及Apollo合作，目標是促成最多$5,000億的運算投資；執行長Jensen Huang表示，Nvidia可能視個案為一項投資機會提供最多25%的殘值支援。這類支援可讓特殊目的載體以設備與客戶合約為基礎，以較低成本借款。若客戶停止付款，硬體可重新出租或出售，剩餘缺口則由擔保人承擔。債務隨晶片折舊而攤還，通常約5年，擔保金額也隨時間下降；不過，客戶違約與硬體價值下跌同時發生時，這項保障才最有價值。

既有架構顯示曝險規模及轉移方式各不相同。Meta在路易斯安那州Hyperion資料中心約$270億融資，以及德州Sopaipilla專案約$130億融資中提供殘值支援；相關義務與Meta選擇提前退出長期租約連結。Broadcom則將此概念用於晶片融資，為替Anthropic客製晶片提供資金的$350億Big Sky交易承擔大部分擔保。Bank of America策略師估計，至2029年中，更廣泛的AI XPV平台可能累積$3,700億優先債務。S&P在調整後槓桿中，將Broadcom的支援視為類似債務的或有義務；Moody's則警告，即使帳面債務仍低，短期內進行多筆交易仍可能削弱財務彈性。

這項變化比又一則大型AI發債消息更具影響力。目前已有約$700億此類或有支援未列入大型企業帳面債務，隨晶片融資擴張，金額可能繼續增加。景氣繁榮時，擔保可促進銷售並降低客戶融資成本，幾乎不需立即支出現金；景氣急遽下行時，卻可能在晶片商獲利轉弱、二手設備價值下跌之際，將損失重新拉回晶片商的資產負債表。因此，信用市場關注的問題正從AI能否取得融資，轉向評等、利差與文件條款是否充分反映客戶、硬體與擔保人之間的相關尾端風險。

$22.5億Zenith Arc綠色債券，反映較傳統專案目前的融資價格。5年期Ba2債券以99.5定價，殖利率近9%，位於先前討論區間較寬的一端；即使有Jane Street子公司15年期三重淨租賃，以及慣常的Jane Street Group擔保，定價仍然偏寬。租約將營運支出、稅負、公用事業費、保險與電力成本轉由承租人負擔，卻未消除建造、技術或集中度風險。偏寬定價與投資級債訂單流失數據一致：AI基礎建設仍能取得資金，但當槓桿與專案風險位於最強企業資產負債表之外，投資人會保留應有補償。

## 擔保品、重整與主權資產負債表

較低評級信用更清楚呈現價值如何在不同利害關係人之間轉移。Arini Capital Management與GoldenTree Asset Management擴大對Liberty Puerto Rico的訴訟，挑戰5月簽訂的$1.4億循環信貸與$2億定期貸款。債權人指控，這些融資以9月債務管理操作中移入非限制子公司的資產作擔保。此前交易將公司大部分資產移出既有貸款人可追索範圍，並用來擔保Diameter Capital Partners提供的$2.5億新債。AllianceBernstein關係企業、Octagon Credit Investors與MacKay Shields現已加入紐約州最高法院訴訟。

修正後的訴狀不只涉及單一再融資爭議。債權人另指出，一筆公司間貸款遭無償取消，以及5月發行的$5億特別股可能每年向Liberty Latin America股東支付$4,500萬股利。其經濟主張是，公司以移轉後的擔保品籌措新融資，同時將資產與現金流受償順位從既有貸款人手中移走。最終法律認定將影響債務管理文件，因為這套架構在同一串受爭議交易中，結合了非限制子公司空間、順位優先債務、股東分配與母公司誘因。

其他借款人選擇以股權修復槓桿，而非移轉擔保品。Dangote Sugar透過超額認購的現金增資，以每股60奈拉發行81億股，籌得4,860億奈拉，即$3.56億。這家奈及利亞生產商計畫降低債務、補回連續3年虧損耗損的資本，並為營運與向後整合專案提供資金。2023年奈拉貶值推高融資與投入成本，使公司在復甦前陷入負股東權益，造成資產負債表受損。此處股權稀釋提高了對債權人的償付能力，而非透過新增債務抽取價值。

Kedrion Biopharma則朝相反方向發展。這家由Permira持有的血漿療法公司正考慮約20億歐元私募債務，部分所得擬用於向包括Abu Dhabi Investment Authority在內的股東發放股利。Kedrion營收超過15億歐元，但交易條件與最終決定仍在討論。私募貸款機構在長期併購低潮後握有大量現金，這筆潛在交易將檢驗資金究竟用於支持生產性擴張，還是為股東分配而提高槓桿。兩者的差異將決定股利發放後留給債權人的緩衝。

主權借款人也利用利差收窄，同時設法降低再融資風險。肯亞計畫在12月底前發行$8.15億歐洲債券，作為截至2027年6月、總額$54億外部融資計畫的一部分。整體方案另包括$3億熊貓債、$5億伊斯蘭債券，以及與世界糧食計畫署進行、由美國國際開發金融公司支持的$10億債換糧食交易。財政部長John Mbadi也計畫償還至少$5億高成本外債。對國際貨幣基金列為高度債務困境風險的主權國家而言，債務管理安排與新增資金規模同等重要。

印尼則形成當前財政政策的對照。總統Prabowo Subianto將2027年赤字目標定為GDP的2.4%，低於2026年預估2.85%；同時提議支出增加4%至4,097兆印尼盾，收入成長7%。計畫假設匯率為17,500印尼盾、原油價格為$75。上半年政府支出成長近30%，帶動GDP成長5.45%，創13年來最強上半年表現，因此赤字下降取決於執行成效，不能只看表面上的節制。市場週五反應正面，印尼盾與股市上漲，債券殖利率下降；但去年赤字目標已被上修至接近3%的法定上限。可信度考驗在於，採購節省、國營企業股利與收入成長，能否支應政府的糧食、能源、教育與鄉村計畫，而無須再次修正目標。

中國則呈現不同的資產負債表訊號：公共債券融資擴張之際，私人信用需求正在收縮。7月借款人對實體經濟的本幣貸款淨償還5,900億元人民幣，創2002年有數據以來最大收縮；包括金融機構間信用在內的整體貸款減少3,400億元人民幣，降幅超過預期的3倍。社會融資規模仍增加1.4兆元人民幣，但政府債券發行占1.3兆元人民幣。家庭與企業中長期貸款均告收縮。這種結構顯示，房地產需求疲弱、薪資停滯與預期報酬偏低促使民間去槓桿，政府融資正在取代而非帶動私人借款。

中國人民銀行同時操作3,490億元人民幣隔夜逆回購，淨投放3,480億元人民幣，為首次於月中使用該天期工具。央行此前未進行其他公開市場資金投放，本次操作旨在滿足繳稅期流動性需求，並不代表轉向全面寬鬆。中國10年期公債殖利率下降1個基點至1.68%，創2025年7月以來最低；10年期公債標售殖利率亦創逾1年最低。另一筆1兆元人民幣、6個月期買斷式逆回購，僅抵銷等額到期。精準的短期流動性支援可穩定融資並強化息差交易，但本身無法扭轉私人貸款需求創紀錄的收縮。

## 前瞻市場意義

接下來的美國通膨與勞動數據，必須判斷7月消費放緩是否持續到足以壓過新一輪能源壓力。8月26日核心PCE、此前公布的就業證據，以及Kevin Warsh在Jackson Hole的談話，將顯示有利的通膨月份是否正如Goolsbee所要求般持續累積。若零售需求持續疲弱、服務通膨溫和且招聘轉弱，即使長端仍昂貴，政策敏感度也將集中於2年至5年期殖利率。若消費反彈或價格壓力擴大，7月主張升息的反對票將重新發揮影響力，週五實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率同步上升，也將成為新一輪政策重定價的起點，而非油價造成的短暫中斷。

伊朗風險須出現實際結果，通膨降溫論點才能重新取得主導。荷姆茲海峽持續通行、運費與保險成本下降，加上原油回吐1週漲幅，將減輕損益兩平通膨率與原油進口國主權殖利率曲線的壓力。若執法加強、制裁實質限制出口，或軍事干擾再起，7月生產者能源與物流成本下降將只具回顧意義。美國2年期殖利率與10年期損益兩平通膨率同步上升，代表能源風險再度進入聯準會政策路徑；若曲線趨陡但短端穩定，壓力仍集中於期限補償與財政存續期間。

週三$160億20年期美國公債標售，是近期最直接的長存續期間融資定價檢驗。30年期公債以5.216%完成標售，加上週五收盤曲線在消費疲弱下仍趨陡，20年期債券接近標售時的發行前殖利率約為5.27%。若得標結果接近標前水準，且次級市場交易穩定，將顯示絕對殖利率即使處於歷史高檔，需求仍然存在。若出現明顯標售尾差，或標售後曲線再次趨陡，則表示公司債發行預期降溫，仍不足以緩解美國財政赤字、全球主權債供給與AI資本支出對資金的結構性競爭。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 14 U.S. fixed-income close rejected the easiest interpretation of weak consumer data. The 2-year Treasury yield finished 2 basis points higher at 4.17%, the 5-year rose 4 basis points to 4.36%, the 10-year increased 5 basis points to 4.68%, and the 30-year added 4 basis points to 5.25%. The 2s10s curve steepened 3 basis points to 51 and 2s30s widened 2 basis points to 108. July retail sales and August consumer sentiment initially reduced the prospect of an imminent Federal Reserve increase, briefly taking the 2-year yield below 4.10%, but that policy relief did not survive a renewed oil shock or the market's continuing demand for compensation to hold fiscal duration.

The composition of the selloff identifies the conflict. July retail sales fell 0.6%, the largest decline since May 2025, with five of 13 categories lower; preliminary University of Michigan sentiment dropped to 51 against a 55 consensus. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee welcomed the recent inflation improvement and supported patience, while insisting that several more favorable months are needed after inflation spent five or six months moving the wrong way. Those developments weakened the near-term tightening case. Yet WTI rose 1.42% to $82.40 and Brent gained 1.67% to $88.52 after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent promised unprecedented economic pressure on Iran alongside the continuing blockade of its ports. The 10-year breakeven rose 3 basis points to 2.27% and the 10-year real yield increased 2 basis points to 2.41%. Both inflation compensation and the real discount rate therefore pushed nominal yields higher.

This was a bear steepening with two different messages, not evidence that the growth data were irrelevant. The short end remained sensitive to weaker spending and hiring, and September tightening expectations fell substantially from late July. Longer maturities had to absorb an energy premium, a still-elevated inflation destination, and a fiscal clearing-price problem that survived the week's adequately covered 10- and 30-year auctions. The 30-year yield is now 17 basis points higher over 1 month, compared with a 1-basis-point decline in the 2-year yield, and the 2s30s curve has steepened 18 basis points over that interval. A softer immediate Fed path is coexisting with more expensive long-run capital.

Credit remained functional but showed sharper price discipline. Investment-grade borrowers had issued $136 billion over the previous two weeks, and investors withdrew 36% of initial orders on average as syndicates tightened final pricing, twice the prior week's attrition and well above the 22% annual average. Thursday's 45% attrition was the highest of 2026. At the same time, funds received almost $3 billion and average high-grade spreads remained near 78 basis points over Treasuries. The message is not capital flight. It is that investors still have cash but are less willing to surrender concession when sovereign yields, AI infrastructure and acquisition finance are all competing for the same balance sheet.

That distinction extends into lower-quality and structured credit. AI financing is migrating beyond ordinary corporate debt into project bonds and special-purpose vehicles supported by residual-value guarantees that can become obligations during an industry downturn. Elsewhere, Liberty Puerto Rico creditors widened a legal challenge to financing secured by assets they say had been moved beyond their reach, and several borrowers pursued equity, asset sales or restructuring rather than relying on inexpensive refinancing. The session's rise in Treasury yields therefore sits inside a broader repricing of who bears long-duration, technology-obsolescence and collateral-transfer risk. Markets are open; loss allocation is becoming more consequential.

## Weak Consumption Met a Renewed Inflation Shock

The consumer releases weakened the case for near-term tightening in both level and breadth. Retail purchases fell 0.6% in July and were not adjusted for inflation. Online and other non-store sales dropped 2.2%, while motor-vehicle and parts receipts declined 1.8%. Restaurants and bars, the report's only service category, rose 0.5%, preventing the release from becoming a uniformly contractionary signal. The timing also deserves qualification because Amazon moved Prime Day from July last year to June this year, potentially pulling some online spending forward. Even with that distortion, the decline was broad enough to make the consumer look less resilient after a stronger first half.

The University of Michigan's preliminary sentiment index added a separate signal by falling to 51 from a 55 median forecast. Together with disappointing employment data and benign July consumer and producer inflation, the releases accelerated a policy repricing that began on August 7. Short-rate contracts showed only about 8 basis points of tightening for September, down from nearly 19 basis points on July 31, and traders were moving away from more than one increase by mid-2027. The 2-year Treasury's brief fall below 4.10%, its lowest since June 30, was the direct market expression of that change before the afternoon reversal.

Goolsbee supplied a reaction-function framework that validates patience without endorsing complacency. He described the economy and labor market as basically stable and said a continued multi-month fall in retail sales would make him nervous, but inflation remains his primary concern. He was encouraged by the previous three months after five or six unfavorable months and said another three or four readings like June would make him more confident that inflation was returning to 2%. His support for the July hold therefore rests on accumulating confirmation, not on one weak spending report. The Fed had held rates unchanged for a fifth consecutive meeting in July, with three policymakers dissenting in favor of a 25-basis-point increase, so the coalition remains divided even as market pricing shifts toward another pause.

Productivity further complicates the policy signal. Goolsbee noted that productivity had slowed after stronger readings last year and questioned whether that weakness would prove temporary. Faster AI-enabled productivity could permit stronger noninflationary growth, but it could also stimulate enough investment to overheat demand. The same technology cycle is therefore capable of lowering unit costs over time and raising current capital spending, power demand and financing needs. A weak retail month narrows the immediate case for restraint; it does not settle whether the economy's supply capacity is improving fast enough to accommodate the AI investment boom.

Oil prevented that dovish impulse from defining the close. Bessent said the United States would announce measures the following week that were unprecedented in the history of economic isolation, alongside the continuing naval blockade of Iranian ports. Brent ended at $88.52, 5.95% higher over 1 week, and WTI closed at $82.40, up 5.40% over the same period. The U.S. threat arrived before the close and reversed the earlier benefit from weak demand data. Bonds were responding more directly to energy and inflation risk than equities, which declined only modestly: the S&P 500 lost 0.17%, the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.13%, and the VIX dropped 2.60% to 14.25.

The inflation-linked market makes that energy transmission observable. The 10-year breakeven rose 3 basis points to 2.27%, fully reversing the prior day's decline and returning to its August 11 level. The 10-year real yield also rose 2 basis points to 2.41%. The nominal selloff was consequently not just an oil move and not just a term-premium move. Inflation compensation recognized renewed geopolitical pressure on energy, while real yields preserved a high hurdle for capital against substantial public and private borrowing. Gold gained 0.39% to $4,380.40 and the Dollar Index fell 0.29% to 99.67, indicating continued demand for protection without a dollar funding squeeze.

The closing curve reconciles the conflict better than either headline alone. Weak consumption reduced the probability of an immediate Fed increase, but higher oil raised the cost of waiting and fiscal supply kept long maturities heavy. The 5-year yield's 4-basis-point increase and the 10-year's 5-basis-point rise show that the pressure extended beyond the far end. Still, the steeper 2s10s and 2s30s slopes preserve the policy-versus-duration distinction: uncertainty migrated away from the next meeting and into the inflation path, the real cost of capital and the price required to finance long-dated obligations.

## Long Duration Still Clears Only at a High Price

Friday's selloff extended the lesson from the preceding Treasury auctions without replaying their full result. The $42 billion 10-year and $25 billion 30-year sales were absorbed, and the long-bond bid-to-cover ratio was broadly normal, but their awarded yields were the highest since 2007 and 2001, respectively. Market access is intact. The cost of that access is the issue, as a larger debt stock, persistent deficits and a more price-sensitive marginal buyer base require higher compensation even when inflation data temporarily improve.

The 30-year yield at 5.25% finished above the auction's 5.216% stop, and the 10-year returned to 4.68%, almost exactly the level at which its own sale cleared. Over 1 month, the 10-year yield is 10 basis points higher and the 30-year is 17 basis points higher, compared with a 1-basis-point decline at 2 years. The 2s10s slope of 51 basis points and 2s30s slope of 108 basis points are therefore not simply bets on eventual easing. They also embed the extra duration premium demanded when disinflation at the front end does not reduce the government's borrowing requirement.

The real-yield structure confirms the burden. A 2.41% 10-year real yield is 8 basis points higher over 1 month, and the 30-year real yield reached 3.00%, up 13 basis points over that period. Investors are not being compensated only for uncertain inflation; the real discount rate itself has risen as public deficits, AI capital expenditure and global government borrowing compete for savings. A 30-year fixed mortgage rate of 6.69%, the highest since July 2025, shows how that sovereign clearing price transmits into household finance even when the Fed's next move becomes less threatening.

Fitch's AA+ affirmation did not remove the fiscal feedback loop. The agency warned that the deficit relative to GDP would widen in 2026 because of tax cuts and tariff rebates. Fiscal-year-to-date interest expense had reached $1.17 trillion, 15% above the prior year, with higher Treasury yields contributing to the increase. Rising borrowing costs enlarge interest expense, which in turn adds to future financing needs. Treasury's change in debt-management language from evaluating future auction-size "increases" to considering "changes" opened the possibility of less long-bond supply, but no reduction has occurred. Moving more issuance into 2- to 7-year maturities would change duration distribution while increasing refinancing exposure; it would not eliminate the deficit.

Cash activity was substantial enough to make the close meaningful, although it supplies no directional customer-flow conclusion. Treasury turnover totaled $974.5 billion in original-face value, 19.0% below the unusually active prior session. Nominal coupons accounted for $824.4 billion. More than 20-year maturities traded $116.8 billion, 3.3% above the prior day even as overall activity fell, and dealer-to-customer transactions represented 50.7% of that bucket. The long end's higher yield was thus established amid continued two-way transfer of duration rather than an absence of trading.

An upcoming $16 billion 20-year sale will provide the next direct clearing-price observation. The security traded around 5.25% on Friday and indicated near 5.27% in the when-issued market. If the auction awards near that level, it would be the tenor's highest yield since its 2020 reintroduction. The event belongs to the next session rather than the completed close, but its starting point demonstrates how little relief the long end retained from weaker U.S. consumption and reduced September tightening expectations.

## Credit Cash Is Available, but Concession Matters Again

The investment-grade primary market shifted from effortless compression toward visible investor resistance. Average order attrition reached 36% during the week, twice the previous week's rate and 14 percentage points above the 2026 average. Thursday's 45% reading set a yearly high. In AMD's $4.75 billion offering, orders for the longest tranche fell by more than half after the issuer reduced its borrowing cost. That did not prevent execution, but it showed that headline book size overstated final demand once spread was removed.

The supply backdrop explains the change in behavior. Borrowers had placed $136 billion in two weeks, putting August on course to become the busiest August on record, before an expected slowdown to roughly $20 billion in the following week. Acquisition finance and AI infrastructure were arriving alongside ordinary refinancing and a Treasury curve already demanding high real yields. Investors could still absorb the calendar, yet the opportunity cost of accepting minimal concession increased as alternatives multiplied across sovereign, corporate and project debt.

Broad market conditions remained orderly. High-grade funds received almost $3 billion in the week through Wednesday, and average investment-grade spreads were near 78 basis points over Treasuries. HYG and JNK fell only 0.10% and 0.07% on Friday and remained slightly positive over 1 week, while LQD lost 0.40% as benchmark yields rose. Those fund prices cannot establish cash-spread direction, but they are inconsistent with generalized credit liquidation. The better interpretation is a buyers' market at syndication, with duration accounting for much of the weakness in high-grade total returns and issuer-specific terms deciding order retention.

AI financing makes that selectivity structurally important. Nvidia's proposed partnership with Goldman Sachs, Blackstone and Apollo aims to enable as much as $500 billion of computing investment, and Chief Executive Jensen Huang has said Nvidia may provide residual-value support for up to 25% of an opportunity on a case-by-case basis. Such support helps special-purpose vehicles borrow against equipment and customer contracts at lower cost. If a customer stops paying, the hardware can be re-leased or sold; the guarantor covers any remaining shortfall. The debt amortizes as chips depreciate, often over roughly 5 years, reducing the guarantee over time, but the protection becomes most valuable precisely when customer defaults and falling hardware values occur together.

Existing structures show the scale and the different ways exposure can migrate. Meta used residual-value support in a roughly $27 billion financing for its Hyperion data center in Louisiana and a roughly $13 billion package for the Sopaipilla project in Texas, with the obligation linked to its choice to leave long leases early. Broadcom applied the concept to chip finance by backstopping most of the $35 billion Big Sky transaction funding custom chips for Anthropic. Bank of America strategists estimated that the broader AI XPV platform could accumulate $370 billion of senior debt by mid-2029. S&P treats Broadcom's support as a contingent debt-like obligation in adjusted leverage, and Moody's warned that multiple transactions in a short period could reduce financial flexibility even if reported debt remains low.

This is a more consequential delta than another large AI bond headline. Roughly $70 billion of such contingent support already sits outside major companies' reported debt, and the number may grow as chip financing expands. During the boom, guarantees support sales and reduce customer funding costs with little immediate cash expense. In a sharp downturn, they can pull losses back onto chipmakers just as earnings weaken and used-equipment values fall. The credit question is therefore moving from whether AI can obtain financing to whether ratings, spreads and documentation capture correlated tail risk across customers, hardware and guarantors.

The $2.25 billion Zenith Arc green bond illustrates the current clearing price for a more conventional project. The 5-year Ba2 notes priced at 99.5 to yield almost 9%, at the wide end of earlier discussion, despite a 15-year triple-net lease to a Jane Street subsidiary and a customary Jane Street Group guarantee. The lease shifts operating expenses, taxes, utilities, insurance and power costs to the tenant, but it does not remove construction, technology or concentration risk. The wide-end pricing aligns with the high-grade attrition data: capital remains available for AI infrastructure, though investors are preserving compensation when leverage and project risk sit outside the strongest corporate balance sheets.

## Collateral, Restructuring and Sovereign Balance Sheets

Lower-rated credit offered a sharper view of how value can move between stakeholder classes. Arini Capital Management and GoldenTree Asset Management expanded their lawsuit against Liberty Puerto Rico to challenge a $140 million revolver and $200 million term loan agreed in May. The creditors allege that those facilities were secured by assets moved into an unrestricted subsidiary during a September liability-management exercise. That earlier transaction placed most company assets beyond existing lenders' reach to collateralize $250 million of new debt from Diameter Capital Partners. AllianceBernstein affiliates, Octagon Credit Investors and MacKay Shields have now joined the case in New York Supreme Court.

The amended complaint goes beyond a dispute over one refinancing. Creditors also cited cancellation of an intercompany loan without consideration and $500 million of preferred equity issued in May that could pay Liberty Latin America shareholders $45 million of annual dividends. Their economic claim is that assets and cash-flow priority were transferred away from legacy lenders while new financing was raised against the relocated collateral. The eventual legal treatment matters for liability-management documentation because the structure combines unrestricted-subsidiary capacity, priming debt, shareholder distributions and parent-company incentives in one contested sequence.

Other borrowers used equity to repair leverage rather than moving collateral. Dangote Sugar raised 486 billion naira, or $356 million, in an oversubscribed rights issue by placing 8.1 billion shares at 60 naira each. The Nigerian producer intends to reduce debt, restore capital depleted by three years of losses and fund operational and backward-integration projects. The balance-sheet damage followed the 2023 naira devaluation, which increased financing and input costs and pushed the company into negative equity before a recovery. Equity dilution here improves creditor capacity rather than extracting value through additional debt.

Kedrion Biopharma points in the opposite direction. The Permira-owned plasma-therapy company is considering about EUR2 billion of private debt, with part of the proceeds intended for a dividend to owners that include Abu Dhabi Investment Authority. Kedrion generates more than EUR1.5 billion of revenue, but transaction terms and a final decision were still under discussion. In a market where private lenders have abundant cash after a prolonged acquisition drought, the contemplated deal tests whether capital is being used to finance productive expansion or to increase leverage for sponsor distributions. That distinction will determine the cushion left for creditors after the dividend.

Sovereign borrowers are also exploiting tighter spreads while trying to reduce refinancing risk. Kenya plans an $815 million Eurobond by the end of December as part of a $5.4 billion external-financing program through June 2027. The package also includes a $300 million panda bond, a $500 million sukuk and a $1 billion debt-for-food swap with the World Food Programme backed by the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation. Treasury Secretary John Mbadi also plans to retire at least $500 million of high-cost external debt. For a sovereign the International Monetary Fund classifies as at high risk of debt distress, the liability-management component is as important as the new-money amount.

Indonesia provided a current fiscal-policy contrast. President Prabowo Subianto targeted a 2027 deficit of 2.4% of GDP, down from an expected 2.85% in 2026, while proposing a 4% spending increase to 4,097 trillion rupiah and 7% revenue growth. The plan assumes a 17,500 rupiah exchange rate and $75 crude. Government spending had risen almost 30% in the first half and helped produce 5.45% GDP growth, the strongest first-half result in 13 years, so the lower deficit depends on execution rather than restraint in the headline alone. Markets responded favorably on Friday, with the rupiah and stocks higher and bond yields lower, but last year's deficit target had already been revised toward the 3% legal ceiling. The credibility test is whether procurement savings, state-enterprise dividends and revenue growth can fund the government's food, energy, education and village programs without another revision.

China supplied a different balance-sheet signal: private credit demand is contracting even as public bond finance expands. Borrowers net repaid 590 billion yuan of local-currency loans to the real economy in July, the largest contraction in data back to 2002, and overall loans including interfinancial credit fell 340 billion yuan, more than triple the expected decline. Aggregate financing still rose 1.4 trillion yuan, but government bond issuance accounted for 1.3 trillion yuan. Both household and corporate longer-term loans contracted. The composition shows the state replacing rather than crowding in private borrowing as weak property demand, stagnant wages and low expected returns encourage deleveraging.

The People's Bank of China simultaneously used 349 billion yuan of overnight reverse repos, producing a net 348 billion yuan injection and its first mid-month use of that tenor. The operation met tax-payment liquidity demand after the central bank had skipped other open-market additions; it did not represent a broad easing turn. China's 10-year government yield fell 1 basis point to 1.68%, the lowest since July 2025, and a 10-year auction achieved its lowest yield in more than a year. A separate 1 trillion yuan 6-month outright reverse repo merely offset an equal maturity. Precise short-term liquidity support can stabilize funding and reinforce carry, but it does not by itself reverse the record contraction in private loan demand.

## Forward Market Significance

The next U.S. inflation and labor sequence has to determine whether July's consumer slowdown is persistent enough to outweigh renewed energy pressure. Core PCE on August 26, intervening employment evidence and Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks will show whether several favorable inflation months are accumulating in the way Goolsbee requires. Continued weakness in retail demand, tame service inflation and softer hiring would keep policy sensitivity concentrated in 2- to 5-year yields even if the long end remains expensive. A rebound in spending or broader price pressure would restore force to the July dissents and make Friday's rise in both real yields and breakevens the start of a renewed policy repricing rather than an oil-led interruption.

The Iran channel needs a physical outcome before the disinflation thesis can regain authority. Sustained passage through the Strait of Hormuz, lower freight and insurance costs, and crude reversing its 1-week gain would reduce pressure on breakevens and oil-importing sovereign curves. Additional enforcement, sanctions that materially restrict exports, or renewed military disruption would keep July's declines in producer energy and logistics costs backward-looking. The U.S. 2-year yield and the 10-year breakeven moving higher together would indicate that energy is again entering the Fed path; a steeper curve with a stable front end would keep the burden centered on term compensation and fiscal duration.

Wednesday's $16 billion 20-year Treasury auction is the cleanest near-term test of long-duration clearing price. The bond approached the sale near a 5.27% when-issued yield after the 30-year had cleared at 5.216% and the completed Friday curve had steepened despite weak consumption. A result close to the pre-auction level with stable secondary trading would show that demand remains available at historically high absolute yields. A meaningful tail or renewed post-sale steepening would indicate that the expected slowdown in corporate issuance is not enough to relieve the structural competition among Treasury deficits, global sovereign supply and AI capital expenditure.
